utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: May I remind you that the affirmation you made to tell the truth still applies. Thank you. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, witness. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Witness, I have two clarifying questions. Yesterday you repeatedly referred to Buda. What is the given name and family name of Buda?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Budimir Spasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And yesterday also you repeatedly referred to Jova. What is the given name and family name of Jova?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jova Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take you back to Korisa. Yesterday, and that's page 41 of the transcript, you mentioned that seven to eight policemen were removing bodies from a grave. Why do you think these men removing the bodies were policemen?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were wearing police uniforms, so it was -- normally they were police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how far away from these policemen were you when they were removing bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 15 to 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you see in this very moment, because I understand it was in the evening, may have been dark?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them because they kind of built a light there, a fire there. That's why I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correction. The lights of the excavators were turned on, so that's why I could see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did the policemen bring the bodies to?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They loaded one truck; we did the other one, because, as I said, there were two lorries, two trucks, and two excavators.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you describe what you remember about the trucks, how they were looking like.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trucks were big ones. They had refrigerators. Ours was of a red colour, and the refrigerator was white. The other one, I'm not sure about the colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you remember whether the trucks had any licence plates?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You already mentioned that you were also engaging in work. Could you describe what work you were doing that night?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The excavators dug out the corpses, and we loaded them onto the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For clarification, were you working at the same spot where the seven to eight policemen were working or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Korishe, that was the place where they had killed these people. This is where the police and we loaded the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. But you didn't answer my question. I wanted to know within the location of the Korisa, were you working at the same place as the policemen or were you working at another grave?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked separately in different places. They had one truck; we had our truck. They worked with their own group; we worked with our own group.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So and with your own group you were working at a separate grave, then; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who told you what your task was at this second grave?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Buda.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who determined the location of this second grave in the first place?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything, but there, at the place where we worked, there was the excavator and the truck. They didn't move from that place but started working right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My question was maybe not very clear. Do you remember who in the first place, before the grave was dug, determined that this is the location where to dig?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Buda said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And roughly how many corpses were you moving that night?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't count them but around 80 or 90.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if -- what type of clothes were the deceased wearing?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Why do you think they were in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because you could tell civilian clothes from other clothes. They didn't have any uniforms, so they were dressed only in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The bodies which you had to move, were there also some weapons accompanied to these bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In what state were the bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies were in a very decomposed state. They smelt; there was a stench. It was very hard for us to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And these 80 to 90 bodies, where did they go to? Where did you bring them to?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know, because they took us to another place to dig out other bodies. And it was raining, so I don't know where they took the corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. But when you were touching the bodies, what were you doing? Where were you bringing the bodies at Korisa?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We loaded them onto the lorries.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And when you left Korisa, where did the trucks stay?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the same place where we pulled out the corpses. This is where the trucks were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But when you left Korisa that night, were the trucks leaving with you, or did they stay behind?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trucks remained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Approximately what time did you leave Korisa that night?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately at 2.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did you go at 2.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to the place where the garbage of the city was. First it was the excavator who went -- which went there, and then we arrived and started to dig out the corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, could I have P277 brought up on the screen for us, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want you, in a second when the map pops up, to mark where that garbage dump is for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher already to give the witness a pen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you encircle where you believe that the garbage dump is?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. The place where the garbage dump was, was near this -- near the village of Shpinadjinadi.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You've just encircled it. Could you mark a 2 next to your circle, please.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who, if anybody, escorted you on your way from Korisa to the garbage dump?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With my working pals and the police, the police took us there and then they surrounded us to protect us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And what task did you have at the garbage dump?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same thing we did before. First it was the excavator that went there, and then we went with the refrigerator truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This was the same refrigerator truck which you had seen at Korisa, or it was a new one?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was smaller.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: A smaller one. And could you describe the colour and whether it had licence plates, please.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't have licence plates, but it was -- the refrigerator was white, but I think the truck was of a yellow colour, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall what brand the trucks had?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zastava make.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And the brand of the trucks, the refrigerator trucks at Korisa, do you remember this brand as well?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police one. Ours was Nomad 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm asking about the refrigerator truck brand, if you know.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you tendering this marked map, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm intending to tender it at a later point in time, Your Honours. We'll have a couple more markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Okay. As long as we don't lose the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We don't lose the map. This is be the only exhibit until the end of my examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who tasked you at the garbage dump?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Buda.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You mentioned before that Jova was at Korisa. Did you see Jova also at the garbage dump?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was Buda who gave us the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And who pointed out the position of the grave where the excavator had to dig?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the police who told Buda and Jova, and they ordered us where to go and dig out the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how many bodies did you transport from the garbage dump to the excavator?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 30 to 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. And what type of clothes, if any, were the deceased wearing?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dressed in civilian clothes, like the first ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you see any uniforms or weapons that the deceased were having or wearing?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in what state were the bodies at the garbage dump?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The same as ... could you clarify?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as the condition of the first ones. They were decomposed. There was a stench. It was exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when did the works at the garbage dump finish?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At about 4.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So if I understand your testimony correctly, you have told us that you arrived sometime at 9.00 in the evening at Korisa, and at 4.00 in the morning you were done at the garbage dump. Could you tell us, is that a normal -- was that a normal working hour for you in 1999, working throughout the night?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not a normal working time. Usually we worked during the day, not at night, but that night they took us there to work during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On your way back, who, if anybody, escorted you?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jova and Buda, they were in the same truck with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And was any other vehicle escorting you along the way?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were police who escorted us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to ask you, was there another occasion during the NATO air bombardments where you collected bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where was this?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pusto Selo village, above Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you encircle, if you find it on this map, Pusto Selo, please.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please enlarge the map a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I think then we are losing the second circle. That's why the Prosecution proposed to work from a hard copy yesterday. I'm afraid we have to tender this now in order not to lose the second circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is already an exhibit, if I am correct. It's Exhibit P277.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, but the witness has marked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. The witness has now marked an additional marking, number 2, on Exhibit P277.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If this still works and we can tender it in this form, I would tender it under the same number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we will print it, but it is the one exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The system wants another number. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. That's what I thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The system controls us all, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Exhibit P278.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be P00279, respectfully, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we enlarge a little bit the map the witness just asked or the -- should we start afresh now from, I believe it was 276, P276, the unmarked map, or is it possible to take P278 and enlarge it and then tender it as -- excuse me, P279, enlarge it, and then tender it once the witness has made more markings? I'm in the hands of the Court here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will first of all concentrate on getting a satisfactory enlargement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If it would be possible, the Prosecution would be interested to show P279 enlarged. Because at the end of the day, what we are heading for is having markings on one map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I don't think that it is proper to add new markings to exhibits that are already in evidence, because what we get, we don't know what we get. If something has been admitted into evidence, then we would need to have a blank map and then start anew. That is the only proper way to proceed. Then we would know what we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid experiences differ, Mr. Djurdjic. I'm used to having manual maps which several witnesses mark at different times, and it's all one exhibit. And I can assure you that it can be followed in the end. In this case I understand the Prosecution to be proceeding exhibit by exhibit, eventually to reach the situation where the final exhibit will have all the markings on it. And as long as we follow the transcript, we will know exactly what each of them are. And that should then mean that when you come to work on your address at the end of the trial and the Prosecution does and when the Chamber comes to reach a decision, we need only to look at one exhibit to see all the markings. Now, that, as I understand it, is what the Prosecution is intending. I think that you will find that you'll be able to follow that. Please carry on, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, are you on this enlarged map in a position to find and encircle Pusto Selo?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see very well. I'm afraid I will make some mistakes. I can't read the letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we try, with the usher's assistance, to enlarge that a little bit. If the usher could scroll down -- scroll upwards a very little bit so that Prizren is still -- let's say that half of Prizren is cut off.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you find it now? Otherwise, the Prosecution would have a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little bit lower, please. Again, lower, lower. I can't, really -- I can't see them. I'm afraid I would make a mistake and then it won't be admitted, what I'm going to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We would have a hard copy, as I proposed yesterday. I'm in the hands of the ushers whether this is a feasible course of action, since the witness can't recognise ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Yesterday I was told it was not possible. That's why I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What's not possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To work from a hard copy, I was told. If you could please put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please, on this hard-copy map, encircle Pusto Selo, if you've found it.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe since this will be a new exhibit, we will start with the number 1 again, if Your Honours agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll leave it to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. I think we'll start a fresh exhibit because this is a hard copy now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark a 1 next to your circle, please.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, near Pastasele?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And when roughly did you proceed to Pusto Selo? What time of the year was it?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went there around the end of April, maybe early May. I'm not sure. But that was more or less end of April or beginning of May. I don't know the dates. But most probably at the end of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Of which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who, if anybody, was escorting you on your way there?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our boss Buda and some policemen from Prizren. They took us outside Rahovec, and they -- there was another company of the Hygiene of Rahovec that came with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did you recognise any of the policemen in or around Pusto Selo?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, with the exception of Jova's son who was also a policeman. He was the son of our director. His name was Mirko. He was the only one I recognised. The others I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you state the full name of Mirko, please?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who tasked you when you were arriving in Pusto Selo?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Budimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What did he task you with?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived there, there were other workers from the Hygiene company, also workers from Rahovec. Our task was just to carry the bodies to the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how many bodies did you carry on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 90 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in what state were these 90 bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were decomposed. They had probably been buried a long time before we dug them out, but I don't know exactly the time when they were buried. However, the bodies were decomposed, and there was a stench.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Where were these bodies transported to after you had left them in the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Prizren morgue. All the bodies, we took them to the Prizren morgue. We unloaded them in the garages of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us, were these bodies ever reburied?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Five or six days after we brought the bodies to Prizren, we were ordered to take all the bodies to Prishtina for autopsy. So within a period of four or five days, we took these bodies to Prishtina for autopsy, and then we returned them to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And after you had returned them to Prizren, were they left in Prizren, or were they buried somewhere?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the bodies were taken to Rahovec, some others to Xerxe, and some others to Dusanov near Prizren. And three bodies were buried in the Prizren cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you, first of all, mark the location where the bodies were buried in Orahovac and circle it on the map.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I mark it here? Because it's clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you mark a 2 next to this circle?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How many bodies were, roughly, buried -- reburied in this Orahovac burial place?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Rahovec, about 30 or 30 [as interpreted] bodies were taken there and about 15 or 16 in Xerxe, and in Dusanov, nine or ten bodies, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you encircle Xerxe now and mark a 3 next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can't read your 3. If you could please mark another 3 next to this circle where you belief Xerxe is.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the record, could you spell Xerxe?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: X-r-c-e.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you now encircle Dusanova?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mark 4 next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now can you encircle roughly where the cemetery in Prizren is?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So shall I encircle Prizren? Because I don't see any other place here. I don't see the cemetery here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Can you mark a 5 next to this, please, next to your circle there.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you told us initially the bodies were exhumed in Pusto Selo, which is marked here as number 1 here on the map. You have explained to us that they were reburied in four locations.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation why these bodies were split up into four groups and why these bodies were not reburied in Pusto Selo where you had taken them in the first place?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know. It was our bosses who knew this best. Our order was -- they ordered us to bury the bodies at Xerxe, Dusanov, Prizren, and Rahovec. They know best why they split them into groups and buried them in different locations, I mean, the directors, the bosses. I have no knowledge why they were taken to different places. Our task was to take the bodies to the locations we were told, and this is what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And this reburial activity, in what month was it taking place and what year?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in which month of 1999?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: April or May, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you tell us approximately when did the policemen, the Serb policemen, leave Hygiene company. You mentioned yesterday that they had moved to Hygiene company in 1999.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When all the Serbs left Kosova, this is when the Serbian police left, too, when NATO entered Kosova, NATO infantry forces. So at that time all the Serbs left Kosova, including the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what month of 1999 was that when NATO entered Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know the month, but I think it was June when NATO entered Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So at around that time the policemen left from the Public Hygiene company in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this point in time, Your Honour. And we would seek to tender the map still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you wish to tender the hard copy map that has now been marked? It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00280, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, do you have some questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I do have some questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gjogaj, my name is Veljko Djurdjic. I'm a member of Mr. Djordjevic's team. I have with me today Ms. Marie O'Leary, but our lead counsel is absent today, Mr. Dragoljub Djordjevic. My first question would be to pick up where we left off yesterday. You marked two uniforms that your bosses wore. That's what you marked for us yesterday. Can you describe both these uniforms for us, please.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The director Jova's uniform was a police uniform, while Budimir Spasic's uniform was an army uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these the same uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not the same uniforms. As I said earlier, Jova was wearing a police uniform, while Buda, an army uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you be more specific about the difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jova's uniform was a police uniform, blue camouflage uniform, while Buda had a regular army uniform usually worn by reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gjogaj, when was the last time you saw an image containing these uniforms that you recognised before yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably know that this is the third time that I appear here as a witness before the Tribunal. I've also been a witness before the court in Belgrade. And these are the same uniforms that I've pointed out in both courts. I have completed regular army service in 1984, 1985, and I know uniforms very well, and I can recognise different uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, please listen to me carefully and try to answer my question and nothing but my question to avoid wasting time. As I said, you were shown yesterday this photograph with these uniforms. Prior to seeing the uniforms in that photograph yesterday, when was the last time you set eyes on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999, when they were worn by my director and my boss.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, I asked you prior to yesterday, when were you last shown that same photograph, not when you actually saw the scene played out live, as it were.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no choice but to tell you this. You are not telling the truth, sir. I'm saying this based on the fact that the Prosecutor informed us that on the 28th of January, 2009, you were shown a photograph with uniforms. This is pre-trial Exhibit 05162, an image, a photograph, containing four uniforms, two of them marked with an X. And you were the person who marked the Xs back in 1999 when you were talking to an investigator of The Hague Tribunal in Prizren. Is that true, what I'm suggesting to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course during the preparations for this testimony I saw these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you say so straight away, then?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought you were asking me of the time when I last saw the uniform as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Therefore, it's true that the photograph already bore markings in relation to the uniforms that you identified; right?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gjogaj, can you tell me whether your recollection of the event that you described is better now, clearer now, than it was when you first related your story to the investigator of this International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that I left out details about the event, but at the time I told things as they happened. I told the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question was, is your recollection of the events clearer now than it was back in 1999 when you first gave that statement? Which is clearer?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was back then when it was clearer, the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gjogaj. That's as much as I thought. I am, however, surprised that after nearly ten years, yesterday and today happened to be the first time that you told us about certain facts that you had never addressed before. Let me draw up a quick summary for you of the facts that I have in mind. First of all, you tell us that your director was wearing a uniform during the war, a fact you never mentioned to the investigators or, indeed, this Trial Chamber or, indeed, this Tribunal. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've always mentioned this detail. The director, of course, was wearing police clothes, and I've mentioned this detail at all times. This is a fact. He was wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Fine. We can go through all of your statements, then. You never mentioned before this statement that you were accompanied by Director Jova to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand where to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So what you're suggesting is that you said all these things before; right?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always said that Jova and Buda were with us, because nobody would dare go and do the job we did at night-time at that time. So Buda and Jova were always there, and the police escort, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, all I asked was about Director Jova, not about Buda. Do you still maintain that you said earlier on as well that Director Jova was at the firing range with you?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is bound to come up later on again. Mr. Gjogaj, where did you attend elementary school?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Leshan village, Suhareka municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about your classmates? Were they children of different ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were of different ethnicities, but at that time things were more normal. We lived in harmony in school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday and in earlier statements you said that you were an Ashkalin. Does that make any difference at all?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ashkali are those who do not speak the Roma language. They all fall within Roma as ethnicity, but Ashkalis do not speak the Roma language, so that's why I feel as an Ashkali but, of course, as part of the Roma ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would I be right to say that Albanian is your real mother tongue?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us before about serving your military term; where and when?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I served my military term in Sarajevo in 1984, 1985.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what sort of uniform you were wearing during your regular military term?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The olive-green/grey uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it the same type of uniform worn by Buda during the war?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So what is the difference between the uniform you wore and the one he wore?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was a soldier, my uniform was a plain olive-green/grey colour, while Buda's uniform was a camouflage one, the one that the army wore during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were the kind of uniform that you had during your military term being used during the war as well?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some among the reservists, military reservists, of the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that you were working with a company called Hygijena. Was that gainful employment?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was your salary regular?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, regular.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When the shelling started, were you mobilised into units of the civil protection?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As a member of the civil protection, did you in fact continue to perform your daily duties, as usual, at the Hygijena company?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Before I was mobilised and issued with the uniform of civil protection, I worked as a cleaner on the streets; we collected the garbage. But afterwards we were mobilised, and we were given uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you describe the uniforms that you were given as a member of the civil protection?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were green.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What exactly did the uniforms comprise?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trousers, the jacket, and the cap.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you have a shirt too?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about your boss, Budimir Spasic? Was he mobilised into a civil protection unit as well?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Buda had a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, that's not what I asked you. I asked you if Budimir Spasic, too, had been mobilised into the civilian protection, whether he also worked there in the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not issued the uniform of the civilian protection, but he did accompany us on the ground at all times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And he did his regular job, the job that he did in Hygijena; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question. I didn't hear it, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question. Your boss, Budimir Spasic, did his regular work in Hygijena on a daily basis, just as you did?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did his regular job. We did what he ordered us to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And he received his salary from Hygijena, just as you did, for the work that he did.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gjogaj, let us now try and explain where this Hygijena, this company, is actually located. You are familiar with Prizren, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Hygijena firm is on the west side of the city, where the road to Albania goes. At the end of this bridge, there is the Hygijena company or firm, west of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gjogaj, but this is all rather abstract when we tell the Trial Chamber and the Prosecutor that it's in the western part of Prizren. Your company is on the road leading to Vrbnica, to the border crossing; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: About 1 kilometre before the place where your company is, if you move down the road, since there is a slight slope, there is the district court in Prizren, and then there is the building of the Prizren SUP; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Is it correct that after the air-strikes started, because of the danger caused by the air-strikes, that the Prizren SUP was relocated to several locations?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think that the SUP was where I thought it was. Whether there were or not police inside this, I don't know. Whether SUP was placed to another place, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, I know that the building remained where it was before, but do you know that the people from the building left it and worked in other buildings around Prizren, for instance, in the Putnik Hotel, in the water management company, in the Pristinska Banka building next to the Theranda Hotel, and in some other locations?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw some police at Putnik Hotel because I could see them going to work, because I could say that on my way to work in Hygijena. But as to why they were there, they were established there or did something, this I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that in your company those police officers did their regular work during the war?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that there is a large parking lot in front of your company and that all of your vehicles, vehicles belonging to the company, were actually parked there?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that there was a guard who did not allow anyone to enter the company compound, allowing only those vehicles who were entitled to the access to pass through?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I correct when I say that you don't really know what kind of work the police did, the police that used the offices in your company?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a fact that I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gjogaj, now I would like to move on to what we were talking about today, Pusto Selo, in fact. Mr. Gjogaj, am I correct when I say that you were taken to Pusto Selo by your boss, Budimir Spasic?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was not only myself. It was not only myself; there were others as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true, is it true that you were in a group of workers led by Budimir Spasic and that you went to Pusto Selo together with the police?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you went to Pusto Selo in day-time?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that your colleagues from Orahovac also came together with you to Pusto Selo, those people who joined you in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that on the 24th of June or, rather, on the 27th and the 1st of March, 1999, when you were giving your statement to an investigator of the International Tribunal, you did not know Mirko's last name? That was the son of your boss.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I started working, of course I didn't know. Then afterwards I learned that through my colleagues, that he was Jova's son. And since Jova's last name was Vujicic, so I presume that his son's last name would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, you were not listening to my question. I will have to ask it again. Please listen carefully. You gave a statement to an investigator of The Hague Tribunal on the 27th of February and the 1st of March, 1999. And on that occasion you stated that you were accompanied by Mirko, who was son of Director Jova who worked in the Prizren SUP as a police officer, and you said that you didn't know his last name. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I then conclude that at that time you did not know Jova's last name?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, because it was only the beginning of my work. I was a new worker there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about February 1999 and the 1st of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm just rising because, if I could advise my learned colleague, the statement taken by the OTP was from 2000, February, and from early March 2000. Because you just mentioned it -- the translation said that the statement was taken in February 1999. At that time the war -- the air war had not even been broken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you to my learned friend. You're entirely right. I would like to correct -- to have all references to 1999 corrected in the transcript to 2000. My learned friend is indeed right, because the investigator took the statement in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, could I mention that we don't alter the record. We rely on what is here stated where it is made clear that you had meant 2000 and not 1999. So the correct position is set out in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, do you remember or do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you ask the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 27th of February, 2000, and on the 1st of March, 2000, did -- or, rather, you gave a statement and you signed that statement. The statement was given to an investigator of the OTP of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. And in that statement you indicated you were accompanied by Mirko, son of Director Jova, who worked in the Prizren SUP as a police officer, whose last name you didn't know.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this is what I'm saying to you. I didn't know Mirko's last name. I mentioned this two or three times. I'm not denying that I didn't know it. What shall I say? And it was normal that after awhile I learned it, because I found out that he was Jova's son and that his last name was Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, in this quote that I just read out, you mentioned not only the son of Director Jova but Director Jova himself, indicating that you did not know his last name.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of my colleagues that Jova's last name was Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have to go back to your additional statement. I think you gave it on the 28th of January, 2001, which was the first time when you mentioned the fact that your director's last name was Vujicic. That was the first time that you mentioned this before this Tribunal or, rather, before the Prosecution. And yesterday and today you stated that in front of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, after the first statement that you gave to an investigator, you gave another one on the 24th of June, 2000, and then in 2002 you testified at the trial of Slobodan Milosevic. Then, in 2006, you testified at the Milutinovic et al trial, and you never mentioned the last name of your director or manager. You did so for the first time on the 28th of January, when you spoke to the Prosecution, and then you repeated that yesterday and today in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that probably they didn't ask me about his last name, so why should I mention him, that name?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, how can I ask you about the last name when you said that you didn't know the last name in 1999?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, in 1999 I didn't know my director's last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, apart from giving statements for the Tribunal, you also gave statements in front of a court in Belgrade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Before you testified in that trial, who proofed you?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me where? I didn't talk with anyone. I received three summons from the Belgrade court, and then the police came and took me right away. I didn't have time for any preparations. So I gave the same statement that I gave here. I shouldn't say -- I couldn't say more things than I had said in the previous statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gjogaj, is it true that in Pusto Selo all the bodies were buried in individual graves?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were, one in each.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: A small digression here. Do you know that Mirko, Jova's son, worked as a crime scene technician in the Prizren SUP? It's the team that goes out to the crime scene when there are some crimes committed, murders or traffic accidents, things of that sort. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know what Mirko did when he was in SUP, but every time he was with us he took photos of the corpses, as he did when he was with us. As to what job he had in SUP, this I don't know. The day he was with us in Pastasele, he took photos of all the corpses, and then they put the corpses in bags.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But now that we have come to the topic of what he did and now that you mention that, in the additional statement you recalled that he did some kind of tests on the hands of the bodies that had been exhumed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that all the bodies that had been exhumed were covered with sheets and blankets?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were already buried in sheets and blankets. When we removed the corpses from the graves, they were in this condition. They were covered in sheets or blankets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that afterwards those bodies that were wrapped up in blankets and sheets, after the police carried out the on-site investigation that some markings were put on the bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that those bodies, once they were put in body-bags, that the bags themselves were numbered, that a number was affixed to each bag?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that all those bodies in bags were taken to Prizren and put in the garage there?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that upon the return from Pristina, from the post mortem, that you put those bodies in a separate place so that they wouldn't get mixed up with the bodies -- with the bags containing the bodies that had not been autopsied yet?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that in Pusto Selo you couldn't see the bodies because they were covered with blankets or sheets and that is why you could not tell the investigator what the bodies had looked like?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. We couldn't see them because they were covered in these blankets and sheets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gjogaj. Is it true that you told the Tribunal investigator that in the morgue in Pristina you learned from a guard there that the police in Prizren had received a court order to examine the bodies?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please explain to me how did you get to Dr. Hidajet Luftija, and that now pertains to your conversation or interview with the investigators?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Hidajet Luftija, he was a doctor there. I know him only as a doctor by sight, but not more than that. He performed the autopsies at the hospital of Prizren, in the morgue. He used to work in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Dr. Hidajet Luftija was an expert -- registered as an expert at the district court in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you said in your statement that Dr. Hidajet did not examine the bodies in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a fact that he did not control these bodies, because we took them in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, should I go on, or is this a good time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if it's convenient, we will break now, and we will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, would I be right to say that you were no witness to this and you don't actually know how the persons came to grieve whose bodies you dug up and then transported to Pusto Selo?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that this I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If I may just latch on to this. You don't know how the persons whose bodies were found at the firing range and the garbage dump were killed, do you?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't know. I don't know who had brought these bodies there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gjogaj, you said that 30 bodies were sent back to Prizren following autopsy and then were taken to Orahovac from there. Did you go to Orahovac yourself and were you actually inside the lorry that was taking the bodies to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt my learned colleague, but I just wanted to point out that you have suggested to this witness that 30 bodies were sent back to Prizren. As far as I have understood the witness's testimony, he said some 90 bodies have been dug up in Pusto Selo, and they all have been brought to Prizren. I'm just -- if you could please clarify this. Here you're suggesting that only 30 of the 90 bodies have been brought from Pastasele to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned friend, I believe the record is not correct. I said that the bodies were brought to Prizren and then 30 of them were taken to Orahovac and buried. I'm asking the witness whether he was in the lorry taking the bodies to Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not clear in my memory, Mr. Djurdjic, but I thought the witness merely said some were then taken to Orahovac for burial. I don't think he gave a specific number, but my memory may be faulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe my learned friend the Prosecutor asked the question and that was the answer provided. I'm nearly certain. But this is not about the figure itself. The gist of my question is, was this witness in Orahovac when the bodies were taken there? Was he actually there for the burial?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we're dealing with some bodies, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I wasn't in Rahovec. I was up to Xerxe in another vehicle because other bodies were buried at Xerxe, but I didn't go to Rahovec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have Exhibit D001-3522. Can we have the photographs from this set, please. Perhaps my assistant could simply check the page numbers. This is page 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, do you recognise the places shown in these photographs?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the first time that I worked in Pastasele. I had never been there before. This could well be the village where we exhumed the bodies, but as I said, this was my first time in Pastasele, and I'm not familiar with the village and this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I know that, but could you please look at photograph number 3 and see if that rings a bell.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall this location. I'm sorry, but I don't recall it. Even if it is Pastasele indeed, I will again like to point out here that that was the first time that I went to Pastasele, on that day to exhume these bodies. You can see graves here on the photograph, and at the location where I was, there weren't any graves. It was like a meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, this strikes me as a number of individual graves, but it's irrelevant since you can't really identify the location. Thank you very much anyway, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can have this exhibit removed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, I would like to move on to a set of questions in relation to the firing range and the garbage dump. In order to speed things along, I will be using your statement to the investigators of The Hague Tribunal, dated the 24th of June, 2000. You probably remember Mr. Arne Kristiansen who was the interviewer who interviewed you. Mr. Gjogaj, is it true that in April 1999, at about 2000 hours, Budimir Spasic came to your flat?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that on that occasion he was accompanied by Shefki Salihu, Xhevdet Mazreku, and Isuf Krasniqi? Shefki Salihu.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shefki Salihu, yes; this is correct. These were my colleagues. We worked together, and they also had the civil protection uniforms, Shefki Salihu, Xhevdet Mazreku, and Isuf Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you were picked up by men in a white Volkswagen van driven by Buda?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you then drove back to your company's headquarters in order to then proceed down the road to Suva Reka? Is it true that at Lubishte, near the police station, you took a right turn and proceeded down a dirt track?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We are talking about the firing range; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Indeed, we are. You then stopped at a place called the firing range; right?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please be asked to observe a pause and answer, since there are two different languages involved in this examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT REPORTER
utterances.text: The last answer is missed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just told by the court reporter she couldn't get the last answer of the witness. If the witness could please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, is it true that you then went to a place called Streliste, the firing range?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, am I right to say that this is an open meadow, a large open area?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it not true that you did not count the bodies that you carried into the lorry?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't count the bodies, but as I stated in my statement and here, there were approximately 80 or 90 bodies. The truck was fully loaded. But in terms of counting, it's a fact that I didn't count the bodies. It was not only me who was loading bodies onto the truck. My colleagues were also doing the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it not true that you saw no wounds on the bodies and that you did not recognise a single body?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it not true that you never saw the bodies that were in the lorry?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what way do you mean I didn't see these bodies? These bodies were exhumed, and we loaded them onto the truck. Of course I saw the bodies. I don't know how to explain this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right. What I mean is this: You said there were two lorries, and you loaded the bodies onto one of those. You did not see the bodies that were in the other lorry - that's what I mean - did you?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see those bodies because it was the Serb police that was involved in this work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that the police provided security for your work?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that you then went to the garbage dump by getting onto a refrigerator truck, and you climbed into the cabin of that truck and then drove there; right?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that you saw no wounds on the bodies that you loaded onto the lorry at the garbage dump, and you did not identify a single body, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does the same thing not apply to the firing range, no wounds that you saw and not a single body that you were able to identify?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that when you finished your job at the garbage dump, Buda drove you back to the company in his Volkswagen and then you all drove home?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gjogaj, I've gone through the whole statement. Not a single reference to your director Jova. This was, as I said, on the 24th of June, 1999. Yesterday and today you've made several references to Jova being with you when you went to the firing range and the garbage dump.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that Jova came for the first time at Streliste, the firing range, and at the garbage dump. He did not accompany us earlier. Only Buda accompanied us on earlier occasions. But that was the first time that he came with us that night, when we worked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. In that case Jova did not go to the firing range with you from Prizren?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Only Buda was in the car with you on your way to the firing range; right? But you told us today, sir, that it was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the speaker's please avoid overlap. The interpreters did not hear counsel's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're, I'm afraid, coming in too quickly with your next question, Mr. Djurdjic, because it's necessary, as we're interpreting into several languages, to go through the process and have the interpretation finished before the next question can be picked up. If you would just watch the screen in front of you, I would suggest. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to take that into account, Your Honours. I do have a belief that the witness both times understood my questions and provided contradictory answers on both occasions. I asked about 1999, the statement from 1999, and said that there was not a single reference to Director Jova in that statement, whereas yesterday and today he suddenly remembered to tell us in the additional statement dated the 28th of January about his departure and his presence at the firing range. So that's what my question was about fundamentally and that's where we started.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you understand me, Mr. Gjogaj?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand you. I earlier mentioned that Jova was at the firing range with us in -- during that night, but he wasn't with us at Pastasele. Only Budimir was with us at Pastasele.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, I am reading back to you your statement dated the 24th of June, 2000, in which you made no reference to Director Jova at the firing range, that being with you on the way to the firing range, being with you on the way back to Prizren, or, indeed, in wearing a uniform, a uniform of any kind. You never mentioned him at all in fact. So what I'm asking you now is, how come that back in 1999 you made not a single reference to him, whereas now over the last three or four days, all of a sudden you're mentioning all these things. That's all I'm asking you. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I wasn't asked about this when I was giving a statement. I do not know exactly the dates when I gave a statement, but I will repeat it again: Jova was with us at the firing range when we exhumed the bodies. He wasn't with us at Pastasele. I hope you understand me. Maybe the investigators didn't ask me if Jova was there or not. Maybe this was asked of me, and it is stated as a fact in some of the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: May I just ask, because the place name Pusto Selo has been a couple of times mentioned in the last page, and each time I noted that, for example, page 38, line 15, it is mentioned as "Pastasele." And 39, line 2, it's also mentioned as "Pastasele." Maybe it can be clarify, I understand -- maybe it can be clarified whether Pusto Selo and Pastasele are the same locations. Otherwise, it looks confusing to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you are seeing the place name in two different languages, Mr. Neuner. That is my understanding of it. But the witness may be able to assist us. Do you want to explore this, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, when you gave your statement on the 27th of February and the 1st of March, 2000, to an investigator, you were talking about your testimony, about Pusto Selo, that village or location.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, this was the first time that I went to this village, whether it was called Pastasele or Pusto Selo, that I don't know. Maybe I gave the name of the village incorrectly, because I didn't know the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But now we have the correct version of the name; is that so?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't want to deal any more with the statements that you gave to the investigators of the ICTY. Now I would like to move on to the statements that you gave in the Milutinovic et al case before this Tribunal, the evidence. Mr. Gjogaj, when we're talking about the camouflage uniforms, will you agree with me that in every shop with hunting and fishing supplies in Prizren, you could purchase before the war a camouflage uniform? It was used by hunters and fishermen when they went out to hunt and fish.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean today, now, or before the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Before the war, before the war. Before 1999, in shops where hunters and fishermen bought their supplies, they could buy the multi-coloured camouflage uniforms, as they called it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speakers are kindly asked not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I didn't see that such uniforms could be bought. Maybe there were, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now tell me, the police officers who worked in the Prizren SUP, what kind of uniforms did they have? I'm talking about the colour.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police uniforms, the same colour that generally police officers wore, blue. Now, I can't tell you the exact colour, but I know very well that you could distinguish immediately the police uniform colour. I don't know if you understand what I'm meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I understand what you're saying, but I wanted to ask you, for instance, you know Milan Djuricic from Prizren. He's a police officer.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When you see a policeman in the street, a policeman from the Prizren SUP, could you please describe the colour of his uniform.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look here, they used to wear all sorts of colours, I mean the police, but the SUP police used the usually uniform. I know that the police uniform colour was camouflage, blue camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And was there another blue uniform that was not camouflage, that was single colour?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. Jova's son, for example, had such a uniform. It was one colour, solid colour. When we were in Pastasele, the director's son, as I said, was with us, Mirko. His uniform was one colour, of one colour. It was a -- even among the police, some of them wore a different colour from the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that as you testified in September 2006 before this Tribunal you stated that the police officers had worn green uniforms with a pattern?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question because I am not sure I understood it right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You testified before this Tribunal in September, the 21st of September, 2006. You stated that the police officers who were at the firing range had worn green camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you ask me about the colour of the uniforms of the people in the shooting range, it was that of the police officers. But those that had surrounded us and protected us, of course I didn't see what colour the uniform was because they simply were there to protect us, serve as our guards. They escorted us to Prizren. Those I can describe what colour their uniform was. It was the same blue colour that our director had. But as to the others, they were about 50 metres away or 60 metres away from where we were working. Those who had surrounded us to protect us, I can't describe the colour of their uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Listen to me carefully, Mr. Gjogaj, to what I'm asking you. I'm reading and I'm telling you that as you testified on the 21st of September, 2006, in the Milutinovic et al case, you stated that the police officers wore a green uniform with a pattern. That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I have said that. I am not saying that I didn't say it. Since you are putting it to me and it is written, maybe I said so. But I may tell you also that I may have forgotten, you know, because the work I used to do was a very difficult job, and it was a job done under pressure, you know. And my mind maybe was not in the right, let's say, place at that moment, so I may have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gjogaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I will have to provide a reference for this question. It's Exhibit D001-0883. That's the transcript from the 21st of September, 2006, page -- page 3729, lines 20 to 25, and page 30, lines 1 through 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gjogaj, I would also like to put to you a portion of the transcript from the Milutinovic et al case from the 21st of September, 2006, where you said when asked by Judge Bonomy that there may have been bodies in the second pit at the firing range but that you were told not to interfere with them, that you were doing your job and they were doing their job.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. This is what they told us: You mind your own work; they have their own work to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gjogaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would have a few clarifying questions. If I could ask that P277 is being brought up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And while this is coming up, it has to do with the first grave with which we were -- about which we were talking yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could enlarge a little bit on the encircled number 1, please. Even a little bit more, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm asking this question here because yesterday and today I've observed a couple of descriptions for this place, and maybe you can help us. I have observed the word "Streliste" being used for that place. I've observed the name "Korishe" being observed for that place. I've observed the formulation of "firing range" being used for that place and also observed the name "shooting range" observed for that place. Could you, having just heard these four formulations, enlighten us briefly where exactly were the two graves?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The graves were in Korishe because this shooting range was not in Korishe. It was below the police check-point. Where I did the first marking, the distance is 10, 15 metres, maybe 20 eventually. The police worked with us in the other place. I worked -- we worked where I marked the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I didn't understand your explanation fully, but first of all is it clear that we are talking about one and the same location where the two graves were?

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which places are you talking me -- are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Without giving it a label right now, the label Koriste, Streliste, firing range or shooting range, are we talking about one location where the two graves were located next to each other? That's how I understood your testimony.

utterances.speaker: ALI GJOGAJ [Resumed]
